title: Following Venice Biennale showcase, David Salle brings AI-assisted works to Paris
summary: Following David Salle’s solo presentation at the Palazzo Cini Gallery during the 61st Venice Biennale earlier this year, this exhibition, held in an intimate space at Thaddaeus Ropac Paris Pantin, reunites the works shown together in Venice. The paintings extend the New York-based artist’s use of artificial intelligence as a tool to unravel and recalibrate the logic of painting. Focusing his AI model on his earlier Tapestry Paintings (1989–91) – a series of works based on 18th-century Imperial Russian tapestries that were themselves interpretations of 16th- and 17th-century Italian oil paintings – Salle creates new paintings that collapse time, medium and place. Though committed to the centuries-old tradition of paint on canvas, Salle has been quick to adopt new technologies into his practice. His recent partnership with AI can be seen, in part, as an act of resistance to the proposition that AI will replace human creativity. Salle has been on the cutting edge

title: War stories from the road: Raindrops Keep Fallin' on My Head
summary: Over the years, I had great fun bringing strange and wonderful ethnographic objects to the cameras at Antiques Roadshow. Ironically, some of the most memorable things I ever saw never made it onto television. This was one of them. I can't remember the city, but I remember the couple. They were conservative, buttoned-up, perfectly respectable-looking people. They arrived at the Tribal Arts table and carefully placed a small, hand-painted square box in front of me. I looked at it and said, "I don't do anything like that." They assured me that I certainly did. So I picked it up. It was a music box, and suddenly it began playing "Raindrops Keep Fallin' on My Head." Then the husband casually mentioned that he was a mortician. In retrospect, that should have been my first warning.

title: MoMA opens major exhibition 'Brancusi: The Artist and His Studio'
summary: The Museum of Modern Art opened Brancusi: The Artist and His Studio, a major exhibition surveying Constantin Brancusi's (1876–1957) sculptural achievements through the lens of his Paris studio at impasse Ronsin, on view from October 25, 2026, through February 27, 2027. For more than 40 years, from 1916 until his death, this studio served as a dynamic environment in which Brancusi lived, worked, entertained friends and clients, and exhibited his sculptures. In this singular context, Brancusi blurred boundaries between abstraction and representation, pedestal and object, and a sculpture and its surroundings.

title: Harriet Whitney Frishmuth's bronze dancers on view in Manhattan
summary: The Syracuse University Art Museum presents “‘And she had a pose that was fascinating’: Harriet Whitney Frishmuth’s Models and Sculptures”, now on view through February 4, 2027 at the Louise and Bernard Palitz Gallery at the Joseph I. Lubin House in midtown Manhattan. In the early twentieth century, Frishmuth earned critical acclaim for her small bronze figures of dancers, caught in motion. Later in her life, she received less attention than some of her peers after moving from New York City to live a private life in Philadelphia. This exhibition marks her first solo exhibition in nearly twenty years, inspired by curator Em Spencer G’26’s Art History graduate capstone project last spring. Bronzes and drawings from the Art Museum’s collection highlight Frishmuth’s dynamic depiction of the human body. Her focus on modern dance and her close relationships with her models, often ballerinas, breaks from the static poses and traditional artist-mode

title: Lee Ufan exhibition opens at Serralves in Porto
summary: Serralves Foundation opened Lee Ufan: Fragments of Infinity, the first major exhibition in Portugal of renowned South Korean-born painter and sculptor Lee Ufan (b. 1936). Set across the expansive 45-acre Serralves Park and the iconic Art Deco Serralves Villa, Fragments of Infinity explores the artist’s groundbreaking approach to blending natural landscapes with architectural environments. The presentation features three outdoor sculptures, strategically installed throughout the Park to frame direct encounters between stone, steel, and the surrounding environment. Inside the Serralves Villa, visitors will experience Lee’s meditative paintings — including a major new site-specific work. Three additional sculptures installed inside the Villa invite viewers to explore the tension between materials and context, challenging the boundaries of space and form. title: The Arkansas Museum of Fine Arts announces 2027 exhibition season
summary: The Arkansas Museum of Fine Arts announced its 2027 exhibition season, which includes Cecil Beaton’s Fashionable World, a celebration of the photographer’s glamorous portraits and fashion work, opening in February. The museum will present Pete Souza: Two Presidents, One Photographer, in partnership with the MacArthur Museum of Arkansas Military History, featuring portraits of Presidents Reagan and Obama. The Delta Triennial, AMFA’s legacy exhibition, returns in June. The season begins in November with The Way Things Go, a film by Swiss conceptual artists Peter Fischli and David Weiss that follows a chain reaction of everyday objects. title: Qatar Museums presents 'Expanded Tradition: Contemporary Craft Practices in Mexico'
summary: This fall, Qatar Museums, the nation’s preeminent institution for art and culture, and Years of Culture, Qatar’s cross-cultural exchange initiative, will present Expanded Tradition. Contemporary Craft Practices in Mexico. The exhibition focuses on a group of artisans rooted in established traditions who are innovating from within and traces the continuity of Mexico's vibrant craft heritage while examining how a new generation of makers is reinterpreting inherited techniques, materials, and forms in response to current contexts. Presented as a headline programme of the Qatar Canada and Mexico 2026 Year of Culture, the exhibition is curated by Ana Elena Mallet, Distinguished Professor at the School of Architecture, Art and Design, Tecnológico de Monterrey. title: Studio Museum announces Turiya Adkins, Timothy Yanick Hunter, and Clifford Prince King as 2026-27 Artists in Residence
summary: The Studio Museum in Harlem today announced that Turiya Adkins, Timothy Yanick Hunter, and Clifford Prince King have been selected as the 2026–27 participants in the Museum's acclaimed Artist-in-Residence program. They join a creative community that has grown over the past half-century to over 150 alumni, including some of the most celebrated artists working today. From November 2026 through October 2027, Adkins, Hunter, and King will receive institutional and material support; individualized studio space and a dedicated lounge in the Museum’s purpose-built home; ongoing interaction with members of the Studio Museum community, including curators and Studio Museum Institute and Expanding the Walls participants; professional development guidance; a culminating exhibition in one of the Museum’s galleries; and an exhibition publication. title: Pippy Houldsworth Gallery presents Sofía Bassi's first European solo exhibition
summary: Pippy Houldsworth Gallery is presenting Floating Between Earth and Sky, the first European solo exhibition of Mexican Surrealist painter Sofía Bassi. A contemporary of Leonora Carrington and Remedios Varo, Bassi's work has been underappreciated outside of her native country. The exhibition brings together paintings, works on paper, and a painted ostrich egg - one of just six examples made by Bassi, and the first time that this part of her practice has been publicly presented. At the centre of the exhibition is the rare and exceptional altarpiece, Caja del tiempo (1970), an iconic example of the artist's contribution to Surrealism. Interested in esoteric knowledge and a personal spiritual iconography, Bassi's paintings exist as windows onto memory, mythology, fear, desire and the vast territories of the subconscious. title: Susan Meiselas exhibition in Paris examines history, memory, and the circulation of images
summary: This exhibition is the first to approach the Nicaragua series from the original angle of the life of images—their circulation, their transformation, and their collective appropriation. It brings together more than a hundred works and objects, including previously unseen photographs, never before exhibited or published. To extend this reflection on the perception of historical fact through the image, four contemporary artistic contributions—by Alfredo Jaar, Arno Fischer & Peter Voigt, Joy Garnett, and Gabriel Pérez-Setright—will present works in dialogue with Meiselas's oeuvre. Susan Meiselas is the 2025 laureate of the Henri Cartier-Bresson Lifetime Achievement Award. Born in 1948 in Baltimore, United States, Susan Meiselas lives and works in New York. title: Hungarian artist Máté Dobokay turns chemical exhaustion into art at Bigaignon
summary: Bigaignon presents, from October 8 to November 14, 2026, Studies in Depletion, the second solo exhibition at the gallery by Hungarian artist Máté Dobokay. Conceived as an extension of his major work Development till Exhaustion, the exhibition continues the artist’s investigation into the material limits of analog photography: the point at which the medium ceases to function, when chemical processes become exhausted, and when the photographic substrate breaks down before reassembling into a new form. Since the origins of photography, time has been one of the medium’s fundamental dimensions. The photosensitive layer records and condenses duration. Máté Dobokay expands this principle of recording into a process in its own right: rather than producing a single image, he makes visible a succession of gradual, interdependent transformations. title: Manor Art Prize exhibition features Dominik Zietlow's kaleidoscopic portrait of Lucerne
summary: Dominik Zietlow (*1988) is being awarded the Manor Art Prize, one of the most important Swiss promotional prizes for the fine arts. Nur die Berge begegnen sich nie (Only the mountains never meet) is the title of the exhibition in which the filmmaker is showing his latest works related to Lucerne. The exhibition title references an old saying: mountains cannot alter their position, whereas people are in a position to encounter one another—also in a metaphorical sense. This approach distinguishes Zietlow as a filmmaker: he creates a space of exchange, listens attentively and observes with empathy. Zietlow grew up in Lucerne, his place of birth, however, is merely the artist's point of departure for his kaleidoscopic city portrait Holz, aus dem die Menschen sind (Wood which people are made of), 2026. On the one hand, the title takes up a sentence by the German philosopher Immanuel Kant: "Out of the crooked timber of humanity, no straight thing was ever made."

title: Mendes Wood DM presents Shota Nakamura's first Belgian solo exhibition
summary: Mendes Wood DM will present seven lakes, Shota Nakamura’s first solo presentation with the gallery and his first solo exhibition in Belgium. The show returns to the desaturated, dreamlike terrain of Nakamura, an artist who works as readily from memory as from observation. The Brussels space, with its fireplaces and separate rooms that distinguish it from a white cube, set Nakamura thinking about scale, and he has approached much of the exhibition through medium and small formats as an antimonumentalist choice. The choice plays on a dialectic built into a foundational premise of landscape painting: outdoor observation is returned to us, in miniature, to be viewed indoors. “With a small painting, you have to physically come closer to it,” he says. “Because of the scale, a very small mark or a slight shift in color can become surprisingly

title: Qatar Museums names renowned curator Azu Nwagbogu the Artistic Director of Tasweer 2027
summary: Qatar Museums (QM) has appointed celebrated Nigerian curator Azu Nwagbogu as the Artistic Director of Tasweer 2027, the fourth edition of QM’s photography biennial and the first to be presented under QM’s future Art Mill Museum. Known for his work organising exhibitions and publishing texts that focus on decolonisation, restitution, and repatriation, the internationally recognised Nwagbogu is a founder of the LagosPhoto Biennale and the founder and director of the African Artists’ Foundation (AAF), a non-profit art space in Lagos that promotes contemporary African art, social justice, and cultural dialogue. title: Changwon Sculpture Biennale 2026 opens under 'Resonance Field' theme
summary: The Changwon Sculpture Biennale 2026 Resonance Field, which opened on September 30, is currently on view through November 15. Hosted and organized by Changwon Special City and the Changwon Cultural Foundation, the Changwon Sculpture Biennale is Korea’s only sculpture biennale. Growing out of the MoonShin International Sculpture Symposium in 2010 and held every two years since 2012, it has functioned as a platform where contemporary sculpture discourse intersects with international currents in sculpture. Running from Wednesday, September 30 to Sunday, November 15, Changwon Sculpture Biennale 2026 brings together 74 teams (81 artists) from 41 cities and regions around the world. title: Hales New York presents Shelley Niro's second solo exhibition 'In Her Lifetime'
summary: Hales is presenting In Her Lifetime, Shelley Niro’s second solo exhibition at the New York gallery. Bringing together a focused selection of photographic works spanning several decades of the artist’s celebrated career, the exhibition explores memory, identity, and contemporary Indigenous life through Niro’s rich use of image, text, and ornament. Coinciding with Niro’s solo exhibition at Centre d’art daphne, Montréal, and her inclusion in the Canadian Pavilion at the 16th Gwangju Biennale, this presentation follows Niro’s recent solo exhibition at the Gorman Museum of Native American Art, UC Davis, and her major touring retrospective, 500 Year Itch, which traveled across the United States and Canada (2023–2025). Works by Niro are recently on view in thematic presentations at the Museum of Modern Art, New York, and the National Gallery

title: Jyll Bradley explores light, queerness, and memory at Pi Artworks
summary: Pi Artworks presents Power of What (Memory Room), Jyll Bradley’s first solo exhibition in the UK since Running and Returning, her major presentation at The Box in Plymouth (2025). In both shows, Bradley has created intimate installations that explore memory and identity through photography from her archive, which she has juxtaposed with recent sculptures. Set against wallpaper created by the artist to reflect patterns and colours associated with the artist’s childhood home, these ‘memory rooms’ offer personal, interior spaces for self-reflection. A new series of solarised self-portraits are being presented alongside sculptures that represent the artist’s physical stance as well as a major work that summons the landscape of her formative years in Kent. title: Exhibition at ai. Gallery brings together six artists to explore haunting, ritual, and postcolonial memory
summary: Spectral Kinship brings together six artists whose works give voice to silenced subjects and explore how suppressed histories and unaccommodated desires are made palpable through sound, ritual, materiality and form. Drawing on Avery Gordon’s account of haunting as a social force that makes the present waver, the exhibition approaches the spectral as a condition of latency: elusive or buried beneath the surface, yet continually seeping across seemingly impermeable temporal and spatial boundaries and reverberating through everyday life. Spanning film, sound, painting, sculpture and kinetic installation, the exhibition attunes to spectral traces and resonances that connect otherwise disparate histories and embodied experience into relation across postcolonial, trans-Asian and trans-tropical sites. title: Frye Art Museum presents 'My Body is a Basket' spotlighting three Indigenous women artists
summary: My Body is a Basket brings together works by Brenda Mallory (Cherokee, born 1955), Danielle Morsette (Suquamish, Shxwhá:y Village, born 1987), and Sara Siestreem (Hanis Coos, born 1976), three contemporary Indigenous women artists working in Washington and Oregon whose practices are rooted in innovation, materiality, and abstraction. Weaving—in unexpected materials and scales, and as a metaphor—connects their diverse approaches, whether in the tight weft of a wool blanket or stapled found fibers. Conceived by Frye Director and Curator of Collections Faith Brower and Guest Curator Asia Tail and presented alongside the nationally touring survey An Indigenous Present, the exhibition connects the broader conversation around Indigenous modern and contemporary art to the Pacific Northwest. title: Iris Eichenberg announces departure from Cranbrook Academy of Art
summary: Cranbrook Academy of Art announced today that Iris Eichenberg, Artist-in-Residence and Head of the Metalsmithing program, will leave the Academy at the end of the 2026–2027 academic year. Eichenberg was appointed Artist-in-Residence and Head of the Metalsmithing program in 2006. She came to Cranbrook after a decade of teaching and leading the Jewelry Department at the Gerrit Rietveld Academie in Amsterdam. During her tenure at Cranbrook, she has helped shape generations of artists working across jewelry, metalsmithing, objects, and contemporary craft. “Iris has expanded our understanding of what metalsmithing can be and what it can become,” said Brandon Little, Maxine and Stuart Frankel Director of Cranbrook Academy of Art. “For more than two decades, she has challenged students to look closely

title: Palestinian Ambassador to Ireland visits IMMA for a preview of the work of six artists from Eltiqa
summary: The Palestinian Ambassador, Dr Jilan Wahba Abdalmajid, visited the Irish Museum of Modern Art (IMMA) today (Thursday 22 October 2026) for a preview of Eltiqa: How to Work Together? an exhibition of artists from Eltiqa, an artist collective from Gaza City curated by The Question of Funding, opening tomorrow (Friday 23 October 2026). The exhibition is a collaboration with Art Jameel and tours to IMMA from Jameel Arts Centre, Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Featuring more than 60 artworks by Mohamed Abusal, Abdel Raouf Al-Ajouri, Mohammed Al-Hawajri, Raed Issa, Dina Matar and Sohail Salem, the exhibition tells the story of a community that continues to overcome years of oppression. For over 20 years, Eltiqa (Arabic for “encounter”) have developed artistic practices together while supporting younger generations of artists in Gaza.

title: Annely Juda Fine Art presents Nicola Turner's first gallery solo exhibition
summary: Annely Juda Fine Art opened its first solo exhibition by Nicola Turner, I Tear Secrets from Your Yielding Flesh. A site-responsive installation made mainly from dark wool and horsehair fills the ground-floor galleries at 16 Hanover Square, extending in a procession-like manner that continues 12 metres up the façade of the Georgian townhouse. In line with Turner's practice, the installation references the fascinating history of the building, whilst touching on myriad issues such as shame associated with the female experience, secret-keeping and the inherent "memory" of materials. A sense of place is fundamental to Turner's work and installations. The history of 16 Hanover Square, a Grade II townhouse built in 1720, plays a key role in shaping this exhibition, with a particular focus on two key historical moments.
